chapter: New York, church bands and early training
title: Hearing the Jenkins band in New York and the Herbert Wright story
summary: He first heard the Jenkins Orphanage band on a New York street, found them decent but hungry, and recalls his friendship with the Patrick cousins and the drummer Herbert Wright.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, did you hear the Jenkins Orchestra Band at that time when you were down there?
No, I never never did hear them. My first time I heard them was in New York.
After you came up to New York?
Well, they were playing marches, and ragtime, and everything else.
No, just one of those things, some of the boys you realized had proper control of their instruments.

But I realized after and I found out when I met Patrick---cousins--- that the boys, they said, we were just more or less interested in trying to hide a few nickles and dimes, so we can have a proper meal.
That goes a long way. That means a whole lot. I don't want to say what I've heard about the group and everything else.

But Patrick's cousins and I were very very good friends, very close together, all brass men were close, and that hurt me ever so much when they said we have to -- in other words, they're saying, in other words, if Herbert Wright did what he did, it wasn't really his fault, 'cause he had a rough time coming up. Herbert Wright, you know who that is?
Herbert Wright was a drummer from Charleston with the 369th --
He was the one who killed -- right -- James Reese.
